articles.title: Former NFL star Mark Sanchez reaches settlement over stabbing altercation
articles.summary: Former QB fought with 69-year-old last October. Fox Sports parted ways with Sanchez over incident. Sanchez was charged over Indianapolis confrontation. Former NFL quarterback and Fox Sports analyst Mark Sanchez has reached an agreement in principle with the truck driver who stabbed him during an…
body: Sanchez was stabbed and pepper sprayed by Perry Tole, who was 69 at the time, during the incident in Indianapolis, where the former New York Jets star was due to cover an NFL game between the Colts and Las Vegas Raiders. Prosecutors said Tole used pepper spray and a knife to defend himself ​after Sanchez attempted to enter ‌his truck during an argument over a parking spot.

Tole suffered “significant injuries to his head, jaw and neck” and ‌was seeking damages for his injuries, according to court documents in the civil case. The incident left Sanchez with stab wounds to his torso, and the former quarterback later said the surgeon who operated on him “saved my life”.

Last month, Sanchez’s lawyers filed a motion to plead guilty to at least one charge in his criminal case; that charge has not been specified. He was charged with one felony count of battery resulting in serious ‌bodily injury, and misdemeanor charges of unauthorized entry of a motor vehicle, public intoxication endangering the life of another, and battery resulting ​in bodily injury. A hearing in Sanchez’s criminal case is scheduled for next month.

articles.title: WNBA moves finals schedule to allow Atlanta Dream to play at larger arena
articles.summary: Game 3 moved up a day to avoid conflict. Dream to host at 17,000-seat State Farm Arena. Potential Game 6 venue remains uncertain. The WNBA has moved up Game 3 of the finals by a day so the Atlanta Dream can host the Golden State Valkyries at State Farm Arena.
body: Game 3 will now take place on Wednesday 21 October. Game 4 will tip off at 1pm ET on Saturday 24 October, two and a half hours earlier than originally scheduled.

The Dream had hoped to play at State Farm Arena, the home of the Atlanta Hawks, which seats more than 17,000 fans, rather than their regular home, Gateway Center Arena, which holds only 3,500. The series begins on Saturday in California.

“We are grateful for the efforts made by numerous stakeholders, including the Dream, the Valkyries, the Hawks, State Farm Arena, and NBC Sports and USA Sports,” WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert said.

“The change of venue dramatically expands the seating capacity and ensures that the Dream will be able to provide an extraordinary atmosphere for the first WNBA finals game to be played in the Atlanta market since 2013. We are pleased that thousands more fans across the Southeast region will have the opportunity to experience the ultimate WNBA action – the WNBA finals – in person.”

articles.title: Flat racing's 'Billy the Kid' wants more than just title
articles.summary: BBC Sport speaks to Billy Loughnane, the prodigy nicknamed 'Billy the Kid' who is set to be named champion jockey on Saturday and targeting a record.
body: Billy Loughnane had never ridden in a professional race this time four years ago.
And, at just 20, he's the youngest person to do so in more than a century - which means he hasn't yet shaken off the nickname "Billy the Kid".
In January 2023, BBC Sport went to visit Loughnane at his family's racing yard in Worcestershire.
As a 16-year-old, he was taking the racing world by storm, racking up more than 20 winners in the first few weeks of the year - temporarily putting him top of the flat jockey standings.

articles.title: PSG's Luis Enrique hopes Man City avoid sanctions
articles.summary: PSG boss Luis Enrique says he was surprised to learn Manchester City had been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules and hopes the club avoid sanctions.
body: Paris St-Germain boss Luis Enrique says he was surprised to learn Manchester City had been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules and hopes the club can avoid sanctions.
City host European champions PSG in the Champions League on Wednesday (20:00 BST) - their first home match since being found guilty of the majority of 115 charges.
"There is a lot of noise around Manchester City and there is often noise around big clubs," said Enrique when asked about City's guilty verdict at a news conference at Etihad Stadium on Tuesday.

"We just have to wait and see what the final decision will be. I hope everything works out well for Manchester City because I think what they have done on the pitch has been incredible over the last few years and they certainly deserved to win on the pitch all the trophies they have won.

articles.title: 🚓Medellín plans a major security operation for the Clásico Paisa
articles.summary: The city of Medellín will host a thrilling edition of the Antioquia derby between Atlético Nacional and Independiente Medellín this Wednesday, with a place in the Copa BetPlay semifinals at stake in a single-leg match at the Atanasio Girardot stadium. Heavy police presence and aerial surveillance.
body: To maintain public order with both sets of supporters in attendance, the Mayor’s Office and the Metropolitan Police have deployed around 900 officers, supported by the Halcón helicopter. The operation includes three strategic security cordons around the stadium and its entrances to prevent fireworks or prohibited items from being brought in, following the incidents at the 2025 final.

Independiente Medellín supporters will occupy the north stand, while Atlético Nacional fans will be in the south and east stands, with both sets of supporters sharing the west stand. Age restrictions for minors have also been set according to the seating area. Nacional’s board issued a strong appeal to its supporters to represent the club with respect and tolerance, showing that the passion of football can be enjoyed in complete peace.

articles.title: McIlroy: LIV Golf was half a good idea
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy believes LIV Golf was "half a good idea, executed poorly" and the breakaway is no longer a threat to the traditional game as it tries to relaunch after filing for bankruptcy.
body: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) ploughed in £3.7bn over four years, luring the likes of Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau away from the PGA Tour, before withdrawing its support this year.

That led to Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the United States with a view to relaunching as LIV 2.0, having received a potential $300m (£227m) backing from BC Partners Capital providing a specified number of players re-sign for the new venture.

Rahm has already announced he will not be continuing and news this week that any player signing up for LIV will be barred from DP World Tour membership and Ryder Cup eligibility has delivered a crippling blow.

"LIV had probably like, half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly," McIlroy told the Bloomberg New Economy forum in New Delhi, where he is playing this week in the DP World India Championship.

articles.title: 'State of the Game' report finds most English clubs living on financial brink
articles.summary: The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) has produced a 'State of the Game' report, which has taken a forensic look at English football over the past 18 months, concluding that the game's finances are dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster.
body: The IFR added that interest and investment from around the world continues to grow within English football, but the underlying foundations of the pyramid are under intense strain and require urgent reform.

Despite over £9bn generated in revenue, 94 per cent of clubs are loss-making, with long-term security being put at risk through excessive short-term spending to keep up with rivals. This, the IFR says, has led to a "dangerous cocktail of rising debt and an over-reliance on owner funding, leaving clubs and their fans at risk".
The report acknowledges that the success of the Premier League has driven economic success, making English football the "richest, best and most deeply competitive in the world".

However, it points to "financial cliff-edges between and within leagues", with the average Premier League club making more than eight times the revenues of an average Championship club, and the system of parachute payments paid by the Premier League to Championship clubs relegated contributing to significant overspend by clubs in the Championship.

articles.title: Zverev celebrates becoming year-end No 1 with Bublik win in Shanghai
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev celebrated becoming the year-end No 1 with a 7-6 (8-6) 4-6 7-6 (7-1) victory over Alexander Bublik to reach the quarter-finals at the Shanghai Masters.
body: Zverev, who won the French Open and US Open this year, never looked 100 per cent comfortable, and admitted his "ankle was acting up" following his win.
The top seed will take on ninth seed Alex de Minaur next after the Australian produced one of his best performances of the year to beat Karen Khachanov in straight sets 6-3 6-4 to advance.

Zverev said: "I'm starting to feel my body more and more, but happy to be through because it was a difficult match. He's been playing amazing tennis this week. I think the most important thing was that I won today."

With current world No 1 Jannik Sinner out for the rest of 2026 due to a knee injury and Carlos Alcaraz unable to overtake Zverev this year, the German was competing for the first time since he clinched the year-end No 1 honours for the first time on Monday.
